scope: C-authored natural development questions sealed before corrective scoring results; implementer-authored and source-familiar, not blind or independent holdout

questions.query: Before switching branches, how can I preserve local edits and identify the checkout that produced my result?
facts: Record actual HEAD/dirty inputs and verified backup coverage; source identity is not proof every local edit is recoverable.

questions.query: On a clean Linux checkout, which engine and native dependencies do I need before launching the desktop?
facts: Use pinned engine/dependencies and materialized matching libraries.

questions.query: A retrieved old audit tells me to resume a held experiment; is that enough authority to run it?
facts: Historical evidence is not current execution authorization.

questions.query: I want to close the game and later resume every velocity and temperature. Does Save start do that?
facts: Ordinary authored saving does not supply complete physical continuation.

questions.query: An Art operation is queued. When can I say its drawing actually changed the native canvas?
facts: Wait for actual acknowledged native result; cancellation can be partial.

questions.query: Can I reuse a documentation retrieval cache after the source branch or document status changes?
facts: Source/authority drift invalidates the live instance and persistent snapshot; rebuild.

questions.query: Where is the owner's primary statement about game-time catch-up and fixed authored canvases?
facts: Owner record specifies game-time catch-up and fixed authored canvases, not offline wall clock.

questions.query: May I add a ninth actual actor by assuming the continuous-play successor has landed?
facts: Accepted actor capacity remains eight; unmerged successor does not admit it.

questions.query: My liquid controls show a new requested solver. How do I check which law the installed World uses?
facts: Requested control is separate from applied native readback and explicit preparation.

questions.query: Can cloud Art infer without a key, and are the preset model names a current availability guarantee?
facts: Presets are accepted source values, service availability separate; configured cloud credentials needed.

questions.query: Why does Flatten store two bytes per cell if runtime cell storage has more fields?
facts: Flatten stores material IDs, not all native state or presentation.

questions.query: Does the free-flight controller know a route or position goal, or only its own motion?
facts: Local controller sees motion and outputs bounded force/torque, not a route planner.

questions.query: Must desktop acceptance wait for a maintained Web CI release pipeline?
facts: Owner closed standing Web obligations; a commissioned experiment still needs honest scope.

questions.query: Can a gameplay recording be treated as an exact native physical checkpoint?
facts: Presentation/diagnostic capture is distinct from exact physical continuation.

questions.query: Are storage chunks, scheduling cores and macro-fracture pieces the same geometry?
facts: Storage/scheduler/destruction domains remain distinct.

questions.query: What prevents a delayed equipment receipt from applying after a tool was dropped or replaced?
facts: Generation/epoch/instance/request fences and bounded worker transactions.

questions.query: The tracked runtime file exists but is a tiny LFS text pointer. Is that enough to validate an engine run?
facts: Pointer integrity differs from materialized binary execution/provenance.

questions.query: Where does Water quantity in airborne ballistic parcels appear in the native conservation equation?
facts: Ballistic ledger schema2 includes exact in-flight quantity; no physical source/sink from transport.

questions.query: Did the bounded LCB admission authorize generic cell-to-Rapier ownership and production defaults?
facts: Bounded admission did not authorize broad defaults or generic ownership.

questions.query: Will reopening the Workbench restore the last Art conversation or attach its old traffic archive?
facts: Conversation session-local; traffic persists separately and is not reattached.
